lines.caption: A customer has many orders, and a report has many expenses. How does Rayfin know which ones go together?
Two decorators, one on each side, and Rayfin builds the link for you.
Hi, I'm Ray! Welcome back to Learn Rayfin with Ray.
Today: when to link your data, the one and many decorators, and what happens when you delete. Let's dive in!
The Expense we built last time stands alone, like an island. For a lot of data, that's all you need.

lines.said: Its category is a fixed list, so the set decorator does the job. And owner underscore I D is plain text from sign-in, not a link.
lines.caption: Its category is a fixed list, so the set decorator does the job. And owner_id is plain text from sign-in, not a link.
Reports are different. People create them, rename them, and file many expenses in each.
Store the report's title on each expense, and a rename means editing them all. One typo, and you've got two reports.
So when people create something and share it, give it its own entity, and link to it.
On the expense, the one decorator points at a single report. A question mark makes it optional: an expense can wait to be filed.
Rayfin adds a column to your expenses for the report's ID: a foreign key. You don't write it yourself.
On the report, the many decorator points back at its expenses. It adds no column.
Both take an arrow that returns the class, so the files can import each other. Use a plain import, not import type.
To file an expense, update it with the report's ID, in an object. The client fills in the foreign key.
The many side is read-only. To move an expense, update the expense, not the report.

lines.said: To read across it, select a dot path like report dot title, and each expense brings its report's title.
lines.caption: To read across it, select a dot path like report.title, and each expense brings its report's title.

lines.said: From the report's side, select expenses dot amount, and each report brings its amounts, ready to add up.
lines.caption: From the report's side, select expenses.amount, and each report brings its amounts, ready to add up.
Now tags. An expense can have many tags, and a tag can be on many expenses.
Rayfin doesn't do many-to-many directly, so you add a join entity with two one decorators.
Each ExpenseTag is one link: this expense, with that tag.

lines.said: It declares its keys to filter by them: each property's name plus underscore I D, holding a U U I D.
lines.caption: It declares its keys to filter by them: each property's name plus _id, holding a UUID.

lines.said: To find an expense's tags, query ExpenseTag by expense underscore I D, and select tag dot name.
lines.caption: To find an expense's tags, query ExpenseTag by expense_id, and select tag.name.
Time for a deep dive! What happens when you delete a report that still has expenses?
Each one decorator is a real foreign key in your database. An expense can't be filed in a report that doesn't exist.
And a report with expenses in it can't be deleted. The delete fails, and tells you why.
Rayfin doesn't cascade, and the one decorator has no option to. For expenses, that's what you want.
They're money someone spent. Deleting a report shouldn't quietly take them with it.
So you decide: move them to another report, or delete them. Then the report deletes.
For tags, delete the ExpenseTag links first.
Here's the same model in Fabricator. Blueprint's Data model view draws a line for each relationship.
Report's expenses show Expense with brackets: many. And ExpenseTag sits in the middle, linked to both.
Pop quiz! You delete a report that still has expenses in it. What happens?
A, its expenses are deleted too. B, they stay, but unfiled. Or C, the delete fails until you move or delete them.
Pause the video, and guess…
It's C! Rayfin doesn't cascade, so the report stays until no expense is filed in it.
Let's recap. What people create and share gets its own entity, linked with the one and many decorators.
Deletes don't cascade, so move or delete what's linked first. And many-to-many takes a join entity.

Then tell me in the comments: what's the entity in the middle called?
